title: Dartmouth's provost warned us about AI cheating—but his own AI use cost him his job
gist: Dartmouth provost Santiago Schnell resigned after an advisory committee found he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in a Washington Post op-ed on AI cheating, even though the publishers required disclosure. Claude logs showed him using the LLM to revise papers, fix code and generate figures, and once asking whether his manuscript showed signatures of AI writing. Dartmouth is still pushing AI adoption, with disclosure as the line leaders must hold.

insights.claim: Santiago Schnell resigned as Dartmouth provost after an advisory committee found he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in his Washington Post op-ed, even though publishers required such disclosure.
insights.speaker: Nate Anderson
insights.so_what: Breaking AI-disclosure rules now costs senior academic leaders their jobs.
